label: copy-phase input j (fed-back echo of j), from the 3rd copied token onward
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is the letter j (j originally at position >= 2, i.e. recall_idx >= 3). It is essentially silent on j during the original phase, on the first two copied tokens (recall_idx <= 2), and on any other input token. Magnitude grows with how deep into the copy the j sits: echoed j at recall_idx 3 gives about 0.1-0.5 of max, and j at the 6th-7th original position gives about 0.9-1.0 of max. Repeated or adjacent j echoes stay strong. The output token, next_out, first_tok and prev tokens have essentially no effect (lift about 1-2x).

issues: No systematic gap found. Test split: P 0.996, R 0.986, F1 0.991, mass recall 0.998, which matches the reported scores.

Missed activations (829 on test, 0.2% of activation mass) are mostly weak (0.01-0.12) j echoes at recall_idx 2 (orig position 1). That class has precision 0.045 and mass recall 0.0015, so adding it would only hurt. The other misses are near-zero spillover on the step after a j. All of it is scattered noise.

False positives (248 on test) are j echoes at recall_idx 3 that stay below threshold. This fits the stated weak onset there: recall_idx==3 covers 92% of the lowest activation quartile and 0% of the top two.
The magnitude claim checks out. recall_idx>=6 covers 69% of the top quartile and 0.03% of the bottom quartile, so activation grows with copy depth.
Phase claims check out. Activation is zero in the original and delimiter phases, and in_tok j carries 100% of the activation mass.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
